title: Lamb Kabsa
tagline: The celebratory version of the national dish — tender lamb over spiced basmati.
intro: Lamb kabsa is the version reserved for guests and gatherings, when a whole shoulder or leg is simmered until falling-apart tender in the aromatic kabsa broth. The lamb's richness deepens the rice, making this the grand centrepiece of feasts, weddings and Eid across the Kingdom.

items: 1.2 kg lamb, on the bone (shoulder or leg pieces)
1 cinnamon stick, 5 cardamom, 5 cloves, 2 bay leaves
500 g (2½ cups) basmati rice, soaked 30 min
3 tbsp fried almonds and pine nuts

method: Brown the onions in oil, then add the garlic, ginger and lamb; sear the meat well.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, spices, dried limes and salt; cook until the oil separates.
Add the water, cover and simmer (or pressure-cook) until the lamb is very tender, about 1½ hours on the stove or 40 minutes under pressure. Remove the lamb; strain and measure about 1 litre of broth.
Broil the lamb briefly for colour if you like.
Cook the drained rice in the measured broth with the saffron: boil, then cover and cook low 15–18 minutes. Rest.
Plate the rice, top with the lamb and garnish with fried nuts, raisins and parsley. Serve with daqoos.
tips: Pressure-cooking the lamb first saves an hour and guarantees tenderness.
Skim the broth before cooking the rice for a cleaner flavour.
toServe: A feast centrepiece — serve with daqoos and fresh salad.
